source: Tibetan Elemental Divination Paintings (2001), White Beryl marriage pp210–223 (PDF211–224), embedded Moonbeams

source_notes.paraphrase: A triad of wedding-timing procedures is defined: destroying the enemy sector, adopting the wealth sector, and marrying within the same sector; each has separate animal/month/day/trigram considerations.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Five mother groups of the bride's animal-year or natal animal-month are matched to specific candidate auspicious wedding years/months; the two applications share one classification table.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: A 12-row lookup maps each bride natal animal-month to a proposed ideal wedding animal-day by the opposed sector (e.g., Tiger month to Monkey day).
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Four bride-natal-trigram groups determine one proposed planet/weekday and current trigram for auspicious marriage timing (Saturn/Saturday, Jupiter/Thursday, Mars/Tuesday, Mercury/Wednesday).
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Marriage partners whose year-signs form a reciprocal seventh-removed relation are assigned a favorable wealth-and-children outcome; the same passage offers seasonally favorable marriage months by natal animal.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Same-animal couples have distinct predictions by specific animal, not a single generic compatibility rule; adjacent mouse/ox, tiger/hare, dragon/snake, horse/sheep, monkey/bird, dog/pig are classified via coincident destiny/body elements.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: The White Beryl nuptial-road divination describes seventeen calculation categories (date, trigrams, mewa, year/month/day/hour, planet/lunar mansion, directional and spiritual contexts, attendants, transportation and seat), versus three broad Moonbeams headings.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: The groom's fourteen-star constellation cycle progresses clockwise from Krttika to Visakha; the bride's progresses anticlockwise through fourteen from Anuradha to Bharani, using birth sign and age to assign wedding-day grades.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Twenty unfavorable nuptial-tie types are enumerated, including claims combining the bride's natal elements, mother’s wedding-time elements, trigrams and mewa; the text proposes rituals, not independently documented reversals.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Nine numeric-square positions are paired with named bridal spirits to produce symbolic good or bad fortune categories for the bride’s departure; there is no independent statistical evidence in the table.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: A 12-row chart warns against bridal departure under the same sign as the bride's birth-year, specifying several alternative historical age-of-death and childlessness claims. These are not medical prognoses.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: The source groups natal year animals into first/middle/last seasonal quartets, assigning comparatively favorable or average marriage ages (first: 18/27; middle: 25/31; last: 24/15).
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: The timing procedure makes the claimed marital outcome depend on the bride's natal sign, groom's sign and the departure animal-month; multiple unfavorable series have different asserted affected people.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Distinct traditional rules claim some numbered lunar days and planetary weekdays unfavorable while Thursdays/Fridays favorable and Monday moderate; these must not be reduced to an unqualified universal calendar rule.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: The source distinguishes wedding departure lunar mansions to avoid from several favorable lunar mansions conditional on the bride's destiny element; planet/constellation rules overlap Indian-derived astrology.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: Moonbeams summarizes a ten-factor electional method as year, mewa, trigram, growth sector, month, day, hour, planet, constellation and local spirit-lords.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: The source enumerates five attendants or roles and selects them according to their elemental relationships and year signs to the couple.
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

source_notes.paraphrase: The wedding transport and seat depend on bridal current trigram, natal elements and directional seat position; the prose and adjacent eight-column chart differ in the fourth trigram label (see T20).
source_notes.source_status: English source testimony, no original Tibetan collation

warnings: Marriage timing is electional, cannot be tested as birth-only personality prediction.
Some ceremonial customs are culturally contingent and should not be recommended as conduct.
Historical mortality claims from this text provide no reliable individualized risk estimate.
When tables give alternatives, preserve them separately and mark absent inputs unknown.
No human validation or runtime promotion established.
